evidence.text: Paychex's FY2027 guidance, set 2026-06-25, explicitly assumes 'no further changes to the Fed funds rate' and on that basis guides interest on funds held for clients DOWN to $195-205m from FY2026's $210.9m; the Fed then HIKED 25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%, its first increase since 2023, with the dot plot at 4.00-4.25% for both year-end 2026 and 2027 and markets pricing a further hike.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the exact line the stock trades on. On 2026-06-24 PAYX beat on both revenue (+12%) and adjusted EPS ($1.32) and fell 1.72% purely because the FY27 guide — of which this interest line was a named drag — sat below the street's ~8%. On 2025-06-25 the FY26 guide took the stock down 9.4%. The baseline's seven reactions are 4 down / 3 up with a 1.72% median, and the down days are guide days.
evidence.why_not_priced: PAYX fell over the five sessions spanning the 16 September hike (sealed run_up_5d_pct -3.91%), so the market read a hiking Fed purely as a small-business demand negative and did not mark up a ~100%-margin float line that the company had guided down on an assumption the hike has now falsified. If this were priced, PAYX would have outperformed payroll peers after 16 September and the client-funds line would appear in the previews; the previews are entirely about hiring freezes. The dollars are deliberately sized small: per the 31 Aug 2025 10-Q the float is $4.98bn available-for-sale against only $775.2m of money-market and restricted cash equivalents, so ~86% of the portfolio reprices on the ladder rather than with Fed funds, making the direct FY27 benefit roughly $2-5m of a $195-205m line. What is worth more than the dollars is that a guided line gets revised the right way on a day the market is braced for the wrong way.
evidence.independence: The FOMC decision itself is a separate primary source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html (2026-09-16). ADP set its own FY27 interest assumptions off 'Fed Funds futures contracts and various forward yield curves as of July 28, 2026' (https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-07-29-ADP-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results), so the whole payroll-float complex is carrying a pre-hike rate assumption, not just Paychex. NOTE: this finding shares the client-funds line with finding 3 below; they are the forward and the trailing leg of the same line and are deliberately signed opposite, not double-counted.

evidence.text: Paychex publishes its own free monthly Small Business Employment Watch, and it covers exactly the June-August quarter about to be reported: June 2026 printed a jobs index of 99.83, the highest since August 2025 and a fourth consecutive monthly improvement, and August printed 99.13, in line with the 2026 year-to-date average of 99.20, with weekly hours growth positive for a sixth straight month — so the 'flat employment levels' assumption underpinning the FY27 guide held through the reported quarter even as the stock lost 9.79% in 20 days on hiring-freeze fear.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Filed as guidance rather than reported_quarter deliberately: on 2026-06-24 this name beat both reported lines and still fell 2.3%, and the sweep row states a reported-quarter beat here is worth close to zero. What this series actually settles is reaffirm-versus-cut on the annual guide, and the guide is what moved the stock -1.72% in June 2026 and -9.4% in June 2025. The counterweight is resolved inside this finding rather than left to argue against it: the index deteriorated WITHIN the quarter, from 99.83 in June to roughly 99.23 in July to 99.13 in August, so the data supports a guide that is reaffirmed and does NOT support one that is raised. Paychex has historically reaffirmed rather than raised at Q1 in any case. That is why this is [sizing note removed].7 and not at the +1.4 a clean reading of the quarter alone would have carried.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown has a named cause and it is a large-cap narrative, not this company's book: PAYX fell 3.9% in a single session on 2026-09-08 on fears that corporate hiring freezes would spread to small business. If the market were weighting Paychex's own client-base index over that narrative, the stock could not have fallen 3.9% in a session in the month after its own index printed a twelve-month high for the first month of the quarter being reported. The August release is at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/PAYX/stable-employment-levels-continue-for-u-s-small-businesses-in-k2eaefz17ugv.html (2026-09-01). Sized modestly because this is a free company press release on an 18-analyst, $41bn name — the opposite of the thin-coverage setup where an unpriced fact moves a stock hard.
evidence.independence: ADP, a direct competitor measuring the same client base, guided US pays per control to 0% to 1% for its FY27 on 2026-07-29 (https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-07-29-ADP-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results) — consistent with flat, not contracting. evidence.text: The Q1 consensus revenue bar of $1.63bn is +5.8% year on year, sitting at the very top of the company's own 5-6% full-year guide, in the single quarter of FY27 carrying the hardest interest-on-funds comparison: Q1 FY26 interest was $47.6m and grew 27% on the Paycor balance step-up, struck with Fed funds at 4.25-4.50% against 3.50-3.75% through this quarter, and the Paycor balance benefit has now lapped.

evidence.why_not_priced: The street's Q1 number is published and the company's annual range is published, but the arithmetic between them — that consensus requires top-of-range growth in the quarter with the largest embedded rate headwind and no remaining acquisition inflation — is not in any preview I found, which all frame the quarter as a hiring-freeze question. evidence.independence: Shares the client-funds line with finding 1 and rests on the same 8-K/10-Q family; it is the trailing-comparison leg where finding 1 is the forward-guide leg, and the two are signed opposite on purpose rather than summed as independent evidence. evidence.text: General Mills' fiscal Q1 2027 ended 2026-08-30, and on 2026-09-08 — nine days after the quarter closed — the company reaffirmed the full FY2027 guide AND disclosed quarter-specific consumption data (Q1 retail dollar sales +2 points versus Q4, 8 of its top 10 categories gaining dollar share, cereal category dollar sales +2 points, taste-forward cereal brands +5 points, base pound volume from -10% at end-FY2025 to +2% at end-FY2026); so the guidance line this stock actually trades on has already been marked to a completed quarter, and a guidance cut on 2026-09-23 would be a reversal 15 days after a post-close reaffirmation.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The closest analogue in the baseline is 2025-09-17 — fiscal Q1 with adjusted EPS -20% in constant currency, organic net sales -3%, gross margin -90bp, and the full-year outlook reaffirmed — which moved the stock -0.77%. The one large positive in the baseline, 2026-07-01 at +8.53%, came from a 17% EPS beat plus a brand-new $3bn savings programme, not from a reaffirmation. And this particular reaffirmation was visibly SOLD: the stock went from $39.26 on 09-03 to $35.96 by 09-10. So the residual value of this finding is only the truncation of the left tail — the market sold it because it wanted a raise, not because it doubts the floor — and it is [sizing note removed].
evidence.why_not_priced: Partially priced and I say so. What is not in the price is the TIMING: the wire copy read 'reaffirms guidance at a conference', which the market treats as a mid-quarter statement, and the quarter had in fact already closed. If the market had read it as a post-close pre-announcement, the stock would not have de-rated a further 8% into the print and the front-expiry straddle would not be 1.8x this name's median realised reaction. The specific observable: an implied event move of 5.55% on a name whose guidance range was marked to the completed quarter a fortnight ago.
evidence.independence: Fiscal-period convention confirmed by the prior-year Q1 release covering the quarter ended 31 August 2025 (https://investors.generalmills.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2025/General-Mills-Reports-Fiscal-2026-First-quarter-Results-and-Reaffirms-Full-year-Outlook/default.aspx). The Q1 consumption detail beyond the press-release text comes from a second write-up of the same fireside chat (https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/general-mills-at-barclays-consumer-conference-growth-push-gains-traction-93CH-4456937), so that detail and finding 2 SHARE the 2026-09-08 event as a source and are two readings of one day.

evidence.text: At the same 2026-09-08 fireside chat management said input-cost inflation is tracking toward the HIGH END of the guided 4-5% range with hedge coverage only 6-9 months out (~9 months on crops), while on the 2026-07-01 call it had already said fiscal 2027 profit is weighted to the second half because 'the impact of inflation net of cost savings is expected to be negative in the first quarter' — so the quarter being reported is the one where cost leverage is worst and the $750m of FY2027 savings has not yet phased in.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This lands INSIDE what the company has already guided, which by construction makes it a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and GIS's own precedent for a bad-margin Q1 with the year reaffirmed is -0.77% (2025-09-17, gross margin 33.9%, down 90bp). The baseline's two largest down reactions, -5.11% (2025-06-25) and -3.06% (2024-12-18), were guidance events rather than pure Q1 margin events. Sized small for that reason.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-08 press release headline was 'reaffirms annual guidance'; the high-end-of-range inflation detail and the 6-9 month hedge window sat in the fireside chat and not in the release, so it travelled through transcript coverage rather than the wire. If it were fully in the price, the 30-day consensus drift would not have gone UP 1.4% (from $0.71 to $0.72) over exactly the window containing that statement. That said, it is inside a guided range, which is why it is sized below one point.
evidence.independence: The first-half cost-savings phasing is independently sourced to the 2026-07-01 earnings call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/01/general-mills-gis-q4-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), a different document and a different date. This finding shares the 2026-09-08 event with finding 1; the two are opposite-signed readings of the same day and are deliberately not double-counted.

evidence.text: The option market is paying an event-implied 5.55% (7.75% front-expiry straddle, 38.3% ATM IV) with a +2.75 put skew on a name whose last seven prints have a median absolute reaction of 3.06% and a maximum of 8.53%, while the short base — 46.0m shares, 8.64% of float, 5.60 days to cover — is already covering from 49.1m, and the entire +8.53% reaction to the 2026-07-01 print has been given back (spot $35.805 against a $40.08 director-grant price on 2026-08-30).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Five of the baseline's seven reactions were negative, but six of seven were inside 5.55% and five of seven were inside 3.5%. evidence.why_not_priced: I am signing against the skew, so I have to say why the option market is wrong about THIS print: the downside being bought is dividend-cut and structural-derating contagion — Campbell's cut its dividend 36% on 2026-09-03 and GIS fell 3.25% the same day, and GIS now yields ~6.8% — but a dividend cut is not an event this print can deliver. If the skew were about the quarter rather than about the payout and the sector, the put/call open-interest ratio would not be 0.55. The counterweight is real and is why this is [sizing note removed].7 rather than 2: the resolved record has a hunter losing 11 points to a large put skew, and a covering short base is a reason to shrink a negative, not a licence to enlarge a positive.
evidence.independence: The Campbell's dividend cut and the same-day GIS move are sourced separately (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/03/campbells-slides-9-36-dividend-cut-general-mills-falls-4-kraft-heinz-drops-3/, 2026-09-03). A 'low bar on seasonality' argument: $0.72 is 23.2% of the $3.10 FY27 midpoint against $0.86 / ~$3.60 = 23.9% for the prior year. The bar is normal for a GIS Q1, not conspicuously low, so I dropped this line rather than sizing it.

A causal, company-specific explanation for the -12.5% 20-day run-up beyond sector de-rating, the Campbell's dividend cut on 09-03, a JPMorgan Sell reiteration and an Evercore target trim to $38 on 09-14: there isn't one, and an unexplained drawdown on a 17-analyst mega-cap is not evidence of over-reaction.

A quantified Q1 FY2027 figure in any primary document not already carried by the wire. There is none; this is a mega-cap with full coverage, which is the reason every size here is small.
